claims.span: Callers see a write that will not land: Nimbrel Relay stalls, batch loaders resend the same envelope, and reads against the same shard begin to time out.

claims.text: Every Nimbrel Ledger release on every platform can refuse an append this way.
claims.span: Every Nimbrel Ledger release on every platform can refuse an append this way.

claims.text: A [`429 - Too Many Requests` reply](https://docs.nimbrel.example/ledger/http-status-codes) is what a Ledger node sends once it has nowhere left to put the work, which is to say once [an append queue or a read queue is full](https://docs.nimbrel.example/ledger/why-appends-are-refused).
claims.span: A [`429 - Too Many Requests` reply](https://docs.nimbrel.example/ledger/http-status-codes) is what a Ledger node sends once it has nowhere left to put the work, which is to say once [an append queue or a read queue is full](https://docs.nimbrel.example/ledger/why-appends-are-refused).

claims.text: There are 3 ways an append draws a 429:
claims.span: There are 3 ways an append draws a 429:

claims.text: The `append` or `system_append` worker pools hold more batches than they have slots for (`nbctl pool status --all`)
claims.span: The `append` or `system_append` worker pools hold more batches than they have slots for (`nbctl pool status --all`)

claims.text: The ingest memory guard has refused the batch (`nbctl guard report ingest --counters`). [1]
claims.span: The ingest memory guard has refused the batch (`nbctl guard report ingest --counters`). [1]

claims.text: A circuit breaker has tripped (`nbctl breaker list --tripped`) - a breaker trips on any operation and is not particular to appends.
claims.span: A circuit breaker has tripped (`nbctl breaker list --tripped`) - a breaker trips on any operation and is not particular to appends.

claims.text: From release 4.6 and release 5.1 onward, appending to a `wide_text` column draws a 429 on its own account whenever the batch would otherwise have run the node out of memory.
claims.span: From release 4.6 and release 5.1 onward, appending to a `wide_text` column draws a 429 on its own account whenever the batch would otherwise have run the node out of memory.

claims.text: Take append and query load off the cluster for long enough that the queues drain and the nodes fall back under their limits.
claims.span: Take append and query load off the cluster for long enough that the queues drain and the nodes fall back under their limits.

claims.text: Where batches carry `wide_text` columns and the cluster runs release 4.6 or release 5.1 or later, send fewer envelopes per batch.
claims.span: Where batches carry `wide_text` columns and the cluster runs release 4.6 or release 5.1 or later, send fewer envelopes per batch.

claims.text: A cluster that refuses appends has been given more work than its hardware can carry, so the answer is hardware: larger nodes (scale up), or more of them (scale out).
claims.span: A cluster that refuses appends has been given more work than its hardware can carry, so the answer is hardware: larger nodes (scale up), or more of them (scale out).

claims.text: Splitting a hot stream over more leader shards spreads append load across more nodes, which helps in some layouts.
claims.span: Splitting a hot stream over more leader shards spreads append load across more nodes, which helps in some layouts.

claims.text: Begin by cutting the number of envelopes in each append batch.
claims.span: Begin by cutting the number of envelopes in each append batch.

claims.text: Where smaller batches do not clear it, add processor and memory capacity to the nodes.
claims.span: Where smaller batches do not clear it, add processor and memory capacity to the nodes.

claims.text: Only then raise the `ingest_guard.memory.leader.ceiling` cluster setting, which defaults to 10% of the heap.
claims.span: Only then raise the `ingest_guard.memory.leader.ceiling` cluster setting, which defaults to 10% of the heap.

claims.text: A higher ceiling lets a node hold more in-flight append memory before refusing, and a node holding too much runs out of memory instead of refusing, which is the worse outcome.
claims.span: A higher ceiling lets a node hold more in-flight append memory before refusing, and a node holding too much runs out of memory instead of refusing, which is the worse outcome.

claims.text: The setting is read at startup, so the cluster must be restarted for a change to take.
claims.span: The setting is read at startup, so the cluster must be restarted for a change to take.

claims.text: Where none of that is open to you, the load itself is what changes: fewer appends, cheaper queries, or both.
claims.span: Where none of that is open to you, the load itself is what changes: fewer appends, cheaper queries, or both.

claims.text: Refusals that show up only during a spike usually clear on their own once the queues drain.
